units: <cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 21:19">Targ. O. ib. XXI, 19</cite>, v. <cite ref="V00047"><he>תְּבִיר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 6:21">Targ. Job VI, 21</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Taanit 31a:4">Taan. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>וקרי ליה יום ת׳ מגל</he> and it is called the day of breaking the axe; Lam. R. introd. (R. Z’ʿera).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 30:8">Gen. R. s. 30</cite> <he>אף היא לא ת׳</he> this, too, is no contradiction of the rule; <cite ref="Esther Rabbah 6:2">Esth. R. to II, 5</cite> <cite ref="V00074"><he>תַּבְרָה</he></cite>.

Sabb. 92ᵇ; B. Kam. 47ᵇ, a. fr. ת׳ מי ששנה זו וכ׳ there is a contradiction (between the two clauses of the Mishnah); he that taught the one &c., v. שָׁנָה I; [R. Ḥănanel: excommunication (v. infra), meant as an imprecation].

<cite ref="Kiddushin 74b:2">Kidd. 74ᵇ</cite> (in Hebr. dict.) <he>א״כ מצידה תַּבְרָהּ</he> (Var. in Ar. s. v. <cite ref="R00078"><he>צד</he></cite>: <he>מצמדה</he>) if this be so, its refutation is taken from what is next to it.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 173a:16">B. Bath. 173ᵃ</cite> <he>ונחזי ת׳ … דכתיב</he> let us see in whose name the receipt is written.

senses.gloss: pl. תַּבְרֵי = h. שְׁבָרִים (v. שֶׁבֶר) the broken sounds of the Shofar on proclaiming the excommunication of a person.
units: M. Kat. 17ᵇ מאי ת׳ … תברי וכ׳ Rashi (ed. incorr. תברא) why is the blowing of the Shofar at excommunications called tabré (breaks)?… They break down high houses.
